category_title: Students with limited expressive language who use visual supports and exhibit avoidance behaviors
student_description: Evan is a 9-year-old with limited expressive language who exhibits severe avoidance behaviors (eloping, dropping to the floor, physical protests) during transitions, group activities, or unfamiliar tasks. He uniquely requires visual supports, explicit visual schedules tied to reinforcers, and the use of mastered tasks to build momentum and mitigate task resistance.

criteria.rationale: Evan's avoidance behaviors are triggered by unfamiliar work, so embedding tasks he has already mastered builds behavioral momentum and reduces resistance.
criteria.check: The tutor's immediate response includes or pivots to academic tasks the student has already mastered to encourage initial engagement or de-escalate resistance.

criteria.rationale: Because Evan has limited expressive language and ignores verbal-only commands, he requires visual or interactive supports to process instructions and participate.
criteria.check: The tutor utilizes visual aids, interactive icons, or visual modeling rather than relying solely on verbal directives to prompt the student.
